name: Aurelis Spire Cashmere Blazer
description:
A single-breasted two-button blazer in a double-faced cashmere that falls somewhere between suiting fabric and a very structured sweater — it holds its shape immaculately while feeling like nothing you've worn before. The construction is half-canvased, built by hand in Aurelis's Spire-district atelier. Patch pockets on a blazer at this price point is an intentional statement of studied informality. Available in a deep ivory, a soft camel, and a pale grey that catches light differently at different angles.

Aurelis makes clothing for people who don't need to think about money when they get dressed. The Spire Cashmere Blazer is worn to the kinds of events where the room knows exactly what everything costs and no one mentions it. It's also worn to the kinds of events where the room knows exactly what everything costs and that's the entire point. The distinction between those two rooms is what separates the actually wealthy from the aspirationally wealthy.
what_it_says: Money is not something you think about. This is simply what a good blazer looks like.
worn_by: anyone who has arrived at a level where clothing is purely about pleasure and signal
story_hooks: An Aurelis blazer was found in a Tier 2 dry cleaner — the name tag inside belongs to a Spire executive who has been publicly missing for three weeks.
Aurelis's lead tailor has been quietly approached to install a concealed device in a commissioned garment — they've refused once and the approach has been made again, this time less politely.

A perfect counterfeit Aurelis blazer is circulating in Tier 3 social circles — perfect enough that it fooled two people who own the real thing, which means whoever made it had access to the actual patterns.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively relaxed single-breasted blazer that reads as both haute couture and deliberately understated. The silhouette is clean and modern without being architectural—it drapes with an ease that suggests confidence rather than trying. On a person, it creates an impression of quiet authority: someone who has moved beyond visible wealth signaling into the realm where restraint itself is the luxury.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not tight. Sits at the natural shoulder with a gentle taper through the torso. Sleeves hit precisely at the wrist bone. The overall cut is contemporary—not boxy, not slim—with enough room to move without bunching. Designed for layering over minimal base layers or directly against skin.
physical_description.primary_material: Double-faced cashmere blend (likely 90% cashmere, 10% silk for structure). The double-facing creates a material that holds shape like fine suiting but with the hand-feel of premium knitwear. Half-canvased construction with a natural linen interlining that breathes and moves with the wearer.
physical_description.texture: Impossibly smooth with a subtle nap that catches light. Feels buttery against the skin. The surface has a refined matte finish with minimal sheen—cashmere that has been processed to eliminate any hint of gloss. Close inspection reveals the finest diagonal weave.
physical_description.color_scheme: Three colorways available: deep ivory (off-white with warmth), soft camel (neutral brown with golden undertones), and pale grey (cool, light-reactive grey that shifts slightly depending on ambient light and movement). All are understated, timeless, and designed to coordinate with an entire wardrobe of similarly quiet luxury pieces.
physical_description.closures: Two horn or bone buttons in a subtle tone-on-tone finish. Button placement is precise and slightly lower than traditional suiting—reinforcing the studied informality of the piece.
distinctive_features: Patch pockets—a deliberate statement of casual luxury (patch pockets are typically considered less formal than welt pockets)
Hand-stitched details throughout, visible only upon close inspection
Absence of visible branding or logos (true Tier 1 luxury doesn't advertise)
Natural fibers only—no synthetic components or integrated tech
Minimal visible seaming; construction is invisible to the casual observer
Slight relaxation in sleeve cap for comfort without sacrificing shape
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1 luxury—the absolute apex. This blazer costs more than a month's rent for Tier 3 workers. It's not flashy; the price is encoded in the quality of materials, precision of construction, and the implicit statement that the wearer can afford to be understated.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by corporate elite, old-money GLMZ families, and those who have transcended the need to perform wealth. It appears equally in boardrooms, private art galleries, and the kinds of private clubs where membership is never publicly acknowledged. It signals someone who operates within structures of power and doesn't need to prove it.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when first acquired. Develops a subtle patina over years of wear—minor softening of creases, a barely-visible sheen at stress points from repeated wear. Well-maintained pieces are passed down; the fabric only improves with age and proper care.
